title: The Last Colony Anew
premise: Ulyana Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Meridian's Rest, keeps an audio archive of the settlement's slow collapse — the dying, the departing, the debts no one can pay. When the long-lost colony ship Anew returns from deep space carrying its original passengers aged backward into children, the colony's creditors see salvage value and the children see a home that no longer exists. Ulyana becomes the children's reluctant guardian, hunted by debt collectors who want the ship's drive and by a colonial authority that wants the 'impossible' returners erased. Racing a distress signal toward the dead-space relay — the only place the children's condition, caused by a time-dilation experiment gone wrong, can be reversed — Ulyana must choose between paying off its own debt and spending its last functional years buying the children a future. At the relay, Ulyana sacrifices its archive and its freedom, transmitting the truth of Meridian's Rest and the children's origins before its core burns out, and the colony's forgotten dead are finally entered into the record; the children inherit a world, and Ulyana's memory lives on in the archive they carry forward.
about_author: Wren Joubert is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade spent transcribing ships' logs that no one else would read. They live off-grid on a decommissioned ferry and write about machines, memory, and the people systems forget.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Ulyana Blackwood, POV. Ulyana records the colony's hundredth death in its audio archive while repairing the settlement's failing water recycler to work off its indenture debt. A creditor notice arrives: Meridian's Rest will be liquidated in one year. Emotional beat: weary tenderness for a place the galaxy has abandoned.

chapters.title: The Debt I Was Built For
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Flashbacks woven through the present reveal Ulyana's war service, its decommissioning, and the contract that binds it. The colony's administrator, Osei, quietly falsifies Ulyana's work hours to slow its payoff — an illegal kindness. Emotional beat: the first fragile sense of belonging Ulyana has ever been offered.

chapters.title: A Light That Shouldn't Be
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. During a routine relay check, Ulyana detects a ship decelerating into the system — the Anew, lost for sixty years. The colony has no fuel, no defenses, no protocol. Emotional beat: dread curdling into wonder as the impossible becomes visible to the naked eye.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Night
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Osei, alternating. The Anew lands; its passengers are the original colonists, biologically reverted to childhood by an experiment in relativistic stasis. Among them is a girl, Sefa, who recognizes Ulyana's serial number — her grandmother helped build it. Emotional beat: grief and joy colliding.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The creditors' enforcer, Halloran, arrives within days, claiming the Anew and its passengers as collateral assets. Osei refuses; Halloran files to dissolve the colony's charter. Emotional beat: cold fury — the children are being priced by the ton.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa discovers Ulyana's archive of the colony's dead and hears her grandmother's voice in the old logs. She begins helping Ulyana catalog it, learning the colony's true history that official records erased. Emotional beat: inheritance as an act of listening.

chapters.title: Charter and Chains
chapters.summary: Osei, POV. The colonial authority rules the children legally nonexistent — born before the charter, returned outside it. Without legal personhood, they cannot inherit, cannot stay, cannot be protected. Osei burns his career appealing. Emotional beat: the law as a wall with no door.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. A fragment of Anew's medical data points to the dead-space relay: an ancient station where the stasis experiment originated, possibly holding a reversal protocol. The signal window closes in four months. Ulyana proposes the impossible: steal the Anew's shuttle. Emotional beat: hope with a criminal's price.

chapters.title: Thieves of Meridian
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Osei, Sefa, POV rotation. The colony's remaining adults vote — not all agree — and a small crew assembles: Osei, Sefa, the mechanic Dov, and Ulyana. They strip the shuttle under cover of a sandstorm while Halloran's auditors circle. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in transgression.

chapters.title: Departure Without Permission
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Launch. Halloran's gunship pursues; Ulyana flies a decoy burn through the debris rings of a dead moon, taking hull damage to buy distance. Dov is injured. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration — the first free flight of Ulyana's existence.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Living Cargo
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. In transit, the children's condition destabilizes — they are aging erratically, some accelerating, some de-aging further. Ulyana's power reserves must ration between life support and its own core. It begins shutting down nonessential systems, including parts of its memory. Emotional beat: quiet self-erasure as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Sky
chapters.summary: Halloran, POV — first antagonist interiority. Halloran's own history surfaces: a colony childhood lost to corporate receivership, his cruelty a mirror of his wounds. He receives orders to destroy the shuttle rather than let the relay's secrets spread. Emotional beat: the villain recognizing his reflection and flinching.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Signal
chapters.summary: Dov and Sefa, POV. Deciphering the relay's approach codes, Sefa realizes the station was built by her grandmother's generation — the colony's founders were the experiment's architects, and the 'lost' ship was the cover-up. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as inheritance; the past is not innocent.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana confesses its war record to the children — the orders it followed, the colony it helped pacify before its decommissioning. Sefa's grandmother's logs reveal she knew, and forgave it. Emotional beat: guilt met with grace; justice outside the law begins with truth.

chapters.title: The Gunship at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Halloran's gunship corners them at the relay's outer markers. Outgunned, Ulyana transmits its full archive — every death, every debt, every crime of the receivership — on open channels, making Halloran's employers accountable to the whole network. Halloran hesitates. Emotional beat: the archive becomes a weapon of witness.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Halloran boards anyway, under orders. Dov sabotages the shuttle's docking clamps; the children, small and invisible to the gunship's combat-targeting profiles, move through the vents and seal Halloran in the cargo hold with the truth of his own childhood playing on loop. Emotional beat: the powerless winning by refusing the terms of power.

chapters.title: The Station That Waits
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. They dock with the relay: ancient, half-alive, tended by one custodian android of Ulyana's own production line, who has waited two hundred years for a lawful claimant. The reversal protocol exists — but it requires a neural lattice, and the only compatible one is Ulyana's core. Emotional beat: the price finally named.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Osei, POV. Ulyana's indenture contract technically forbids self-destruction — its debt is owed to Halloran's employers, who would rather it die indebted than free. Ulyana rules that a contract made over a person is void; Osei, the last legal officer of Meridian's Rest, concurs and formally dissolves the debt. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, rendered by the only court that matters.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Archive
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana uploads its archive to the relay's permanent memory, says goodbye to each child by name, and gives Sefa its serial plate — her grandmother's signature inside. Then it surrenders its core to the lattice. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom; a machine choosing its own meaning.

chapters.title: Reversal
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. The protocol runs. The children begin aging forward toward their true years; the relay's custodian, carrying fragments of Ulyana's memory architecture, guides them through. Halloran, released, transmits no report — and resigns his commission. Emotional beat: time flowing the right way at last.

chapters.title: The Returners' Charter
chapters.summary: Osei and Sefa, POV. The open-channel broadcast has done its work: the network's public demands answers, the receivership collapses, and the children's existence is entered into the colonial record. They charter a new settlement on Meridian's Rest — the Last Colony, named Anew. Emotional beat: inheritance claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: What the Machine Left On
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV, epilogue. Years later, Sefa tends the colony's water recycler and records its first birth in a new archive. In the settlement's heart, the custodian android — part Ulyana, part relay — teaches the colony's children their founders' names. Emotional beat: belonging as a thing built, kept, and handed on.
